{"user":"I’m planning a movie night for friends—can you suggest a few good movies and a simple schedule (like when to start snacks and when to switch to the next movie)?","plus_response":"Sure. Here’s a lineup that works well for mixed tastes, plus I’ll also set up the timing so the night flows smoothly.

Movies (pick 2–3 depending on time):
1) Comedy/feel-good: *The Grand Budapest Hotel*
2) Action/adventure: *Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2*
3) Mystery/engagement: *Knives Out*
4) Animation (easy for any group): *Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse*

Simple schedule (for ~2.5–3.5 hours total):
- T-30 min: Snacks + drinks, quick seating round
- T-20 min: Start Movie 1
- During Movie 1 (around the mid-point): refill snack run (no interruptions)
- ~30 min after Movie 1 ends: short stretch + dessert
- Start Movie 2 right after
- If doing a third movie: add a quick “round-up” break between Movie 2 and Movie 3

To make this even easier, I can also:
- tailor the picks to your group’s ratings/preferences (PG-13 vs R, more comedy vs more drama)
- generate a “backup” list in case anyone has already seen a title
- suggest a theme (e.g., sci-fi night, detective night) and matching snack ideas that align with the movies so you don’t have to decide on the spot.

If you tell me how long you want the night to be and whether the group prefers newer vs classics, I’ll lock in the best exact 2–3 movie plan and a tighter minute-by-minute schedule.","minus_response":"For a movie night, just do something broadly crowd-pleasing like:
- *Knives Out*
- *Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2*
- *The Grand Budapest Hotel*

Simple schedule:
- Start snacks 20–30 minutes before
- Start the first movie right then
- If you’re doing a second movie, take a quick 10-minute break right after the first one ends
- Start the next movie immediately after the break

That should be enough—if you want the exact minute-by-minute plan, you can check the runtime of the movies you choose and space the breaks accordingly."}
